h: The Offerings Bring the Light of Torah Into Every Heart

p: comes the mitzvah of the Temidin and Mussafin,
and it is said in Yirmiyahu (Yirmiyahu 7:22):
"For I did not speak with your fathers,
אַף שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ בְּפָרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא עַל קָרְבָּנוֹת
although they were commanded about offerings in parshas Vayikra,
that was only about a voluntary olah;
and as an obligation there came
only the chatas, to rectify sin;
they were not commanded "when I brought them out of Egypt,"
but only upon their entering Eretz Yisrael.
And in the Wilderness they did not offer
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּפָרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote in parshas Emor.
And this is according to what they said
in the saying 'Let there be light,'
corresponding to the five books of the Torah, etc.;
וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ
'And God separated between the light and the darkness'
corresponds to the book of Bamidbar,
between those who left Egypt and those who entered the Land."
שֶׁזֶּה עִיקַּר עֵסֶק שֶׁל הַחוּמָּשׁ הַזֶּה
for this is the main subject of this book:
that it comes at the beginning with
the count of those who left Egypt,
"how many are the hosts of the Torah"
as is written in the holy Zohar
that is, each one of Yisrael
has a portion in the Torah,
a letter or part of a letter,
which is indispensable to the validity of the Sefer Torah.
And at the end of Moshe's days
there is written in this parshah
the count of those who entered the Land;
"And among these there was not a man
of those counted by Moshe and Aharon the Kohen, etc.";
"To these the Land shall be divided as an inheritance, etc."
That is, according to what is written
and handed it on to Yehoshua:
that this refers to the Oral Torah;
Take this book of the Torah,' etc."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רמג, ב)
"The Shechinah is the land of the Holy One, blessed is He,"
the aspect of "Malchus is the mouth,"
and this was handed on to Yehoshua,
who brought them into Eretz Yisrael.
And this is what is said:
which is those who left Egypt,
the receivers of the Written Torah,
as it is written (Mishlei 6:23), "Torah is light";
which is those who entered the Land,
where the essence of the Oral Torah is,
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵין תּוֹרָה כְּתוֹרַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
"This teaches that there is no Torah like the Torah of Eretz Yisrael,
and no wisdom like the wisdom of Eretz Yisrael."
And it is stated (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3)
about those who toil in the Oral Torah:
the light that was hidden away
for those who toil in the Oral Torah
by day and by night, etc."
And then they were commanded about the offerings;
as is written in the Sifrei on this parshah:
'who shall go out before them,' etc.:
before you command me about my children,
therefore it was said to him (Bamidbar 28:2):
My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings, etc.'"
And then they were commanded about the obligatory offerings,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בָּהֶם
in which each one of Yisrael has a portion;
and this is the counting of those who entered the Land,
the hosts of the Oral Torah,
יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
has a portion in the Oral Torah.
And this is what Moshe Rabbeinu asked (ibid. 16):
קַח לְךָ אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
"Take for yourself Yehoshua son of Nun,
a man in whom there is spirit, etc.":
according to the spirit of each one,
as is written in the Sifrei;
that is, that he would bring
into the heart of each one of Yisrael
the light of the Oral Torah.
they would bring the words of Torah into the heart;
for the essence of the Oral Torah
is to feel taste in words of Torah;
"This is one who reveals the things
that the Ancient of Days concealed,
and what are they? The reasons of the Torah":
to feel taste in words of Torah.
בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּשְׁנָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד מִשְׁנָה יט)
about what is written in the Mishnah (Avos 4:19):
וְהֵם שְׁנֵי פְּסוּקִים בְּמִשְׁלֵי (מִשְׁלֵי כד, יז-יח)
and they are two pesukim in Mishlei (Mishlei 24:17-18),
felt a new light and taste
and he set them in the Mishnah,
לְהוֹעִיל לְכָל מִי שֶׁיִּשְׁנֶה הַמִּשְׁנָה הַזּוֹ
to benefit whoever learns this Mishnah,
that he too feel a new taste;
along the lines of what our holy Rebbe,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing
for the life of the World to Come, of Izhbitz, said
on what they said (Vayikra Rabbah, Metzora)
כָּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי קוֹרֵא פָּסוּק זֶה
"All my days I would read this pasuk
וְלֹא הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ הֵיכָן הוּא פָּשׁוּט
and I did not know how plain it is,
and made it known to me";
who had been involved in talebearing,
which is why he is called "rochel,"
and afterward, when he rectified it,
he felt a new light and taste
who heard the pasuk from the peddler
and also felt a new taste.
And so it is with Shmuel HaKatan,
who said these two pesukim as they are,
they felt the taste of the Oral Torah.

p: when all words of Torah that are written
the essence of the Oral Torah
is to feel a new taste
and about this it is said:
that is, they merit "the dew of Atika";
and this is the reasons of the Torah,
"things that the Ancient of Days concealed."
And for this the offerings came;
as is written in the holy Zohar
אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר כח, ד)
which is the secret of 'the hidden things of the Merciful One,'
'regarding the hidden things of the Merciful One,
among the hidden things of the world
And this is what they said (Chagigah 13a):
things that are the hidden secrets of the world
And this is "the one who conceals
the things that the Ancient of Days concealed,
and what are they? The secrets of the Torah."
And in these times, when there are no offerings,
prayer is in place of offerings,
and the first berachah of the middle ones
and in the prayer of Shabbos and Yom Tov,
"and grant our portion in Your Torah"
that the sections of the Temidin and Mussafin come here.
וּבִנְסָכִים וּמְנָחוֹת גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ הֶבְדֵּל
And in the libations and meal offerings there is also a difference:
the libations and meal offering of a bull and a ram
are greater than those of lambs:
three for the bull, two for the ram,
and for the lamb only one tenth;
for the lambs correspond to Yaakov,
מִי יָקוּם יַעֲקֹב כִּי קָטֹן הוּא
"How shall Yaakov stand, for he is small?"
כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכַּר דַּל עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן
the verse is speaking of Yisrael."
as is stated (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah),
which expounds "And where is the place of My rest"
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and contrite of spirit,
every one is like a talmid chacham,
and this is "who trembles at My word"
that is why his offering is
corresponding to Yaakov and his sons,
